title: Repeatability of two thickness gauges
intro:
Two thickness gauges each measured the same reference block many times. Gauge A: n₁ = 15 readings with standard deviation s₁ = 0.042 mm. Gauge B: n₂ = 13 readings with s₂ = 0.025 mm. Do the gauges differ in repeatability, that is, in variance? Test H₀: σ₁² = σ₂² against H₁: σ₁² ≠ σ₂² at α = 0.05 with the **F-test**, F = s₁²/s₂² (gauge A on top).

Find F and the two-sided p-value. Give F to two decimals and p to three decimals or more.

Statistic.says: That is the ratio of the standard deviations, s₁/s₂. F compares variances: square each standard deviation first.
That is s₂²/s₁², gauge B on top. The exercise puts gauge A (sample 1) on top: F = s₁²/s₂².

PValue.says: That is a one-tailed p-value. H₁ is two-sided (≠), so double the tail beyond F.

hints: F compares variances, so square the standard deviations first: F = s₁²/s₂².
Under H₀, F follows an F distribution with n₁ − 1 = 14 and n₂ − 1 = 12 degrees of freedom.
Two-sided: p = 2 × P(F₁₄,₁₂ > F) when F > 1. Python 2 * stats.f.sf(F, 14, 12), R 2 * pf(F, 14, 12, lower.tail = FALSE).
